title: Executive Summary
headline: The horizon runs the full three days after a day roll: 34 games from 15 to 18 November 2026, each one re-read from the official date cards and cross-checked against the standings page read in the same window. The 2026-11-14 slate is settled against official finals - 3-10 on the 13 gradable picks, -5.80 units at the repo's -110 convention, with 4 rows left ungraded because no per-player box score is citable - and every published pick now carries a hash, a before-tip attestation and a settlement stamp on the page. Home court is finally a measurement rather than a constant, and it disagrees with the constant by a factor of more than two.
lead:
Ten strategies were written, seven validation gates were defined, and all ten were run against a strictly out-of-sample window: all 65 completed games from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-14, every one predicted using team ratings computed only from 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05, so no game in the test window contributes to the ratings that predict it. On top of that the system originates a line for every game in the next three days - 15, 16, 17 and 18 November - from official ratings and the newest official injury report, now the 11/15/26 06:15 AM ET edition, diffed against the 06:00 AM edition published fifteen minutes earlier.

What the last twenty-four hours changed is procedural, and it matters more than any single line. The injury report the site had been reading was PM-only: the league republishes its report every 15 minutes from 12:00 a.m. ET, and the index parser only accepted names ending in PM, so a morning run walked past the newest edition of the day. That is fixed, unit-checked and gated (F74). The picks table and the settlement ledger, which previously lived in separate files and agreed on nothing, are now wired: each row carries a settled flag, the final, the distance to its own published line and the git blob it was graded against. And home court - until today a hard-coded 2.5-point assumption - has been pinned to the measured league home-win rate, 0.5294 on 187 home games in the standings and 0.5469 on the 64 non-neutral games in our own results feed, which converts to 1.053 points under the model's margin spread. The published lines still use 2.5, because they are frozen and hashed and re-pricing a line after tip would void the pre-registration; the pin takes effect at the next freeze, and the sensitivity of every un-tipped row is printed instead of being applied quietly (F71, Q22).

What did not become possible: travel distance is still not in the model. The term, the great-circle arithmetic and the data contract are all written and self-checked, but no NBA-operated page reachable from this build publishes arena coordinates, and coordinates copied from memory would be untraceable numbers in a table whose entire purpose is traceability. So the coefficient stays 0.0, and the only travel fact the official cards do state - whether a team's next game is in the city it is already in - is published in its place, with the gap named beside it (F70, SG31).

verdict.one_line: The model beats the naive reference on margin accuracy (MAE 12.98 against 13.62) and loses to it on totals (14.83 against 14.72) and on picking winners (42-18 against 40-20). S1 (side edge) is now 23-9, worth +11.91 model units, and for the first time its record is outside what luck alone produces (exact binomial p = 0.020, Wilson lower bound 0.546 against the 0.524 break-even) - but it fails the calibration gate (hit rate 0.719 against a mean predicted 0.627) and the stability gate (the bootstrap interval on the model's margin MAE still overlaps the reference), and the availability gate cannot run at all. Under the tier ceilings it stays a quarter-unit strategy. The 27 new lines are published as lines and paper picks, not as recommendations.
verdict.why: Sixty games with a 17.4-point residual standard deviation have finally made one record statistically distinguishable from a coin flip - and that is exactly when the other gates matter most. A hit rate the model itself did not predict is a calibration failure, not a windfall; an improvement whose interval overlaps the reference is not stable; and a gate that cannot run is not passed. Selective skill means paying for the part that survives every gate and nothing else.

findings.title: The model wins on the margin and loses on totals and winners
findings.detail: Margin: MAE 12.98 against 13.62 for the naive reference, RMSE 17.12 against 17.88 - the model is better on both. Totals: MAE 14.83 against 14.72, RMSE 19.35 against 19.10 - the reference is better on both. Straight up the reference went 42-18 and the model 40-20, and the reference has the better Brier score (0.2001 against 0.2020) and the better log loss (0.5827 against 0.5873).
findings.reading: The refinements buy a real but tiny margin improvement and nothing else. The probability calibration is the weakest part of the model, and it is where the remaining work should go.

findings.title: Growing the window keeps changing what can be claimed - which is the point of the sample gate
findings.detail: On the 28-game window the model beat the reference on totals (MAE 14.50 against 14.75). On 51 games it did not (14.86 against 14.75) - the sign flipped. On the 60-game window the sign holds (14.83 against 14.72) and the gap narrowed, but the conclusion stands. Each addition of data has moved at least one claim.
findings.reading: Any single-window result at this sample size should be treated as a hypothesis, not a finding.

findings.title: S1 has cleared the luck gate at 23-9 - and failed two others, which is the honest headline
findings.detail: S1 (side edge vs the reference spread) produced 32 graded plays at 23-9, worth +11.91 model units and a 37.2% return at -110. Its exact binomial p-value against a coin flip is 0.020 and the Wilson 95% interval on its hit rate is 0.546 to 0.844 - the lower bound is now above the 0.5238 break-even, so G4 (skill, not luck) passes for the first time. But its hit rate of 0.719 against a mean predicted probability of 0.627 fails the calibration gate (gap 0.091 against a 0.08 tolerance), and the stability gate fails because the bootstrap interval on the model's margin MAE (10.2 to 15.94) still contains the reference MAE (13.62). The availability gate cannot run at all for the graded window.
findings.reading: This is what selectively skill-based looks like: one gate says this is probably not luck, two gates say the model does not understand why, and the funding tier stays at quarter unit until every gate that can be run has been run and passed.

findings.title: Home court looks normal; the back-to-back penalty is large but uncertain
findings.detail: Home-court advantage estimates at +3.51 points with a standard error of 2.28 (t = 1.54) across 60 games, squarely in the historical NBA range. The back-to-back penalty estimates at -6.26 points with a standard error of 4.86 (t = -1.29); because |t| >= 1 the model applies the full 6.26, but the standard error is most of the estimate.
findings.reading: Both are published with their standard errors and both are fitted on the test window, which is disclosed on every row they touch.

findings.title: Shrinkage was derived rather than guessed, and the curve is flat where it matters
findings.detail: The empirical-Bayes calculation gives k = 2.9, weighting each team's observed net rating at 0.739. The fixed-k sweep shows margin MAE moving from 13.62 at k = 0 to 12.91 at k = 4, then degrading to 13.36 by k = 20. Heavy shrinkage is clearly wrong; the choice between light and none barely matters.
findings.reading: The constant is defensible, its sensitivity is published, and it is not a source of hidden risk.

findings.title: Availability impact is a measured floor, not an estimate
findings.detail: Minutes are only known for the 50 players in the captured official table. Players outside it contribute 0.00 to the impact, so teams missing rotation players who are not top-50 scorers show a smaller number than the truth - sometimes zero. The minutes-coverage column sits next to every figure so a 0.00 is never read as 'healthy'.
findings.reading: Correct but incomplete - the Injuries page says so on every row rather than hiding it.

findings.title: Correlation is measured where it can be and flagged where it cannot
findings.detail: Thirteen team-statistic pairs were measured directly on all 30 teams from the official advanced table. Net rating explains 87% of the variation in win percentage; pace is nearly unrelated to net rating (r = -0.34, p = 0.063) and assist percentage is unrelated to offensive efficiency (r = 0.02, p = 0.92). The parlay and same-game-parlay correlations that drive pricing are model-derived and labelled as such.
findings.reading: The distinction matters most for parlays, because pricing correlated legs as independent is the classic way to overpay.

findings.title: The word 'edge' on this site does not mean edge against a sportsbook
findings.detail: No sportsbook price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one. The site bets the originated line against a deliberately naive reference model built from the same official ratings. Until real prices are logged, 'units won' means model-vs-naive-model units.
findings.reading: This is the single most important caveat for anyone reading the leaderboard.

findings.title: The 2026-11-13 slate is settled, and it did not go well - which is the system working
findings.detail: Every published paper pick on the 2026-11-13 slate was settled against the official finals captured on 2026-11-14. The seven gated singles went 3-4 (-1.40 units at -110) and all three two-leg parlays lost. The picks were pre-registered: the model blocks in the live file are identical to the copy frozen at 2026-11-13T22:45Z, before tip. The originated margin line was off by 12.39 points on average across the nine games - consistent with the 12.98 MAE on the wider window, and a useful reminder that a night like this is normal at this sample size.
findings.reading: Two gaps closed the same morning: the finals now exist (F13 resolved) and the 18 stale team records were refreshed from the official cards (F14 resolved). Two remain open and are published as such: at the newest injury edition five of the ten teams playing on 11/14 have still not filed, and no edition lists any player for the 11/16 and 11/17 games.

findings.title: The 60-game extension is real, but it cannot be reproduced from this repository alone
findings.detail: The 2026-11-13 finals are captured, transcribed three independent times that all agree 9/9, and used to settle every published 11/13 pick (seven singles 3-4 at -1.40 units, three two-leg parlays 0-3). That part is solid and was recomputed in a separate integration session with the same answer. What is NOT reproducible here is the extended metric: the 51->60 window and the 12.98 vs 13.62 margin MAE depend on a team-ratings refresh, and https://www.nba.com/stats/teams/advanced?Season=2026-27&SeasonType=Regular+Season returns no data table to this environment (flag F24, re-tested 2026-11-14). The committed ratings snapshot is still the one captured at 2026-11-14T00:38Z, whose season-to-date window predates the 11/13 games.
findings.reading: A reader can check every score and every settlement row against NBA.com, and should. The 60-game error metric they cannot check, because the inputs that would produce it are not retrievable. Treat the settlement as verified and the extended error metric as reported-but-not-reproducible until the ratings capture is automated.

findings.title: The game-day edition arrived, and it moved the model far less than it should have
findings.detail: New Orleans, Cleveland, Chicago and Miami filed between the 04:15 AM ET edition the horizon was cut from and the 01:30 PM ET game-day edition, adding 24 player rows and changing four statuses; Memphis was still inside its filing window. Re-run through the engine's own availability adjustment, that edition moves 3 of the 5 games tipping tonight (DAL@CLE -1.8 to -2.5; DET@MIA -12.2 to -12.4; CHI@MIN 30.6 to 33.2) and leaves DEN@NOP, BKN@MEM unchanged. No favourite flips and no published pick changes side.
findings.reading: Two readings are available and the site publishes both. The charitable one: intra-day report churn is usually noise, and a model that lurched on every status label would be worse. The uncomfortable one: the reason it cannot move New Orleans is that the Pelicans' five listed names are not in the minutes table, so the model is not judging them, it is blind to them. That is F47, and it is the highest-value item in the register.

findings.title: Home court, measured: the assumption was more than double the rate the league's own results support
findings.detail: Pinned to the measured home-win rate, home court is 1.053 points (0.5294 on the 187 home games in the official standings HOME column; 0.5469 on the 64 non-neutral games in the committed results feed; sigma 11.0 points). The published lines use 2.5, flagged E-01 as an assumption, and engine/validate.py's in-sample residual intercept says 3.508. The three are printed beside each other on the day-roll page and are not averaged: the disagreement is the finding. Applying the pin to the un-tipped horizon shifts every home margin by -1.447 points, changes no total, and flips the model's favourite on a minority of rows - all of which is published as a sensitivity table rather than applied silently, because the picks are frozen and hashed.
findings.reading: Home court is the single biggest input the site had never measured, and measuring it moves the price of a home team by more than the model's entire shrinkage adjustment. The honest move was to publish the pin, quantify what it would do, and take it up at the next freeze - not to quietly re-price a slate whose picks are already hashed.

findings.title: Settling a slate is now the same act as publishing one, and a losing slate publishes as a losing slate
findings.detail: The 2026-11-14 slate settles 3-10 on the 13 gradable published picks, -5.80 units at the -110 convention, with the parlays 0-2 and four player-prop rows marked not gradable because no allowed host gives this build a per-player box score. Each row links the official date card that published its final, each is graded against the frozen git blob of the picks file rather than the working copy, and the whole set is chained by sha256 (60 hashes, chain head published). One slate of 13 picks is nowhere near evidence of anything, in either direction, and the page says so; the point of the table is that the loss, the ungradable rows and the reason for each are all visible in the same place as the record.
findings.reading: A 3-10 slate against your own number is not a verdict on the model - it is one night inside a distribution with no vig and no market in it. What it does prove is that the settlement path runs end to end: the picks, the hashes, the finals and the graded rows all agree, and the rows that could not be graded say why instead of disappearing.

what_is_live_now: Originated spreads, totals, moneylines and fair prices for the horizon, with the horizon itself rolled today: 34 games across 2026-11-15, 11-16, 11-17 and 11-18, every tip time and record re-read from the official date cards and cross-checked against the standings table read in the same window (30/30 teams agree).

The official per-game result feed for 2026-11-14: one row per game with date, teams, final, OT flag, venue, attendance, officials and quarter scores - 4 of 5 games carry a LINESCORES split and each captured split sums to the printed final; the fifth says 'not captured' rather than being solved backwards (F73).

The official injury report, 11/15/26 06:15 AM ET edition, transcribed row by row (101 rows including the NOT YET SUBMITTED clubs for 11/16), with the report's own revision time and this build's retrieval time both printed on the page, and diffed against the 06:00 AM edition: 0 status changes in the 15 minutes between them, one row whose Team cell the earlier render dropped at a page break.

Settlement of every published paper pick on the 2026-11-14 slate against the official finals, with the pre-registration attestation (git blob 1b962a91275c of docs/data/picks.json), per-row result, distance to the published line, units at the -110 convention, and a 'settled' flag on each of the 60 rows of the picks table so the table and the ledger cannot drift apart.
60 gated picks from the strategy library, each tagged with its strategy, its market, the reference number it is betting against, the model's number and the gap.
Player projections for the top-50 scorers, with the possession, opponent-defence and teammate-availability factors broken out separately.
The settlement of every published paper pick on the 2026-11-13 slate against the official finals, with pre-registration provenance.
Game-flow read-outs built from official pace and efficiency inputs, including probability of a close game, a blowout and overtime.
60 out-of-sample games with the full seven-gate matrix, a 30-team luck decomposition, 13 measured correlations and a ten-strategy leaderboard with reward tiers.

Game-Day Read: the 01:30 PM ET official edition transcribed row by row, the diff against the edition the lines were cut from, the re-priced model line beside the published one for all five 11/14 games, and the 27-of-27 row-level verification of the whole 27-game horizon against NBA.com.

recommended_next_actions.action: Register a citable per-player box-score source and settle the four pending prop rows
recommended_next_actions.why: It is the only thing standing between the prop strategies (S7, S8) and a settled record: the lines exist, the picks exist, the finals exist, and the minutes/production input does not. Parsing the box-score table on each NBA.com game page needs no policy change - same host, already allowed - and it also replaces the estimated minutes column on the props page (F69, Q24, SG32).

recommended_next_actions.action: Adopt the measured home-court pin at the next freeze (Q22, SG30)
recommended_next_actions.why: data/derived/home_court_pin.json is written and reproducible; setting adopted_for_pricing before the next slate's pre-registration is what stops the site pricing home games with a number it publishes as too large. Keep 2.5 published as the pre-change column so the settled window stays interpretable (F71).

recommended_next_actions.action: Add data/official/arena_coordinates.json and fit travel_coef on the 65 completed games
recommended_next_actions.why: The travel term and its arithmetic are already in the model, switched off for lack of input. A published coefficient of 0.0 after fitting would itself be the finding, and would close the brief's travel requirement honestly (F70, SG31).

recommended_next_actions.action: Complete the minutes input, per club, so the availability layer can see a rotation instead of a top-50 slice
recommended_next_actions.why: It is what turns tonight's 0.00 columns into numbers, and it unlocks Q3, Q12 and Q20 (SG20, F47).

recommended_next_actions.action: Automate the day roll behind its own gates (Q25, SG33)
recommended_next_actions.why: scripts/roll_2026_11_15.py already refuses to write unless all 17 freshness and provenance gates pass and merges into the committed snapshots instead of replacing them, so the horizon no longer has to age between sessions.

bottom_line: The machinery works end to end: it originates lines for every game three days out, it tests ten strategies against a real out-of-sample window, it settles the previous slate's paper picks against official finals the morning after, it refuses to promote anything that has not cleared every gate that can be run, and it publishes every gap it cannot close. One strategy has now cleared the luck gate and failed two others - that is the first genuinely selective signal in the project, and the gate matrix is what keeps it honest. What the project still cannot do is prove any of it against a real price, because no NBA-operated source publishes one. The game-day pass added the one thing the site did not have: a measured answer to 'what did we miss by cutting the line before the clubs filed?' - 3 of five games moved, the rest could not, and the reason they could not is a data gap with a name and a size, not bad luck. As of 2026-11-15 the machinery also rolls itself forward and settles itself: 34 games re-read, one slate settled against official finals with the loss published as a loss, 60 hashes chained, the injury report read at its newest edition and diffed against the one before it, and home court measured instead of assumed. What is still missing is narrow and specific - a citable per-player box score and a sourced arena-coordinate table - and both gaps are named on the page that prices with them closed, not papered over.
